clue.text: A container with a type of meat, brought back for His Highness?

indicators.note: something brought back is returned the way it came, so the assembled string is read from the end

parts.note: taken as written
a jar is a container
a ham is a type of meat

explanation.surface: A recipe step: a jar of meat is carried back to serve a royal personage.
explanation.walkthrough: A JAR A HAM, read backwards, gives MAHARAJA.
explanation.definitionFit: A maharaja is an Indian prince, addressed by the honorific 'His Highness', hence the question mark for a definition by example.

clue.text: Brooded on the last of useless vehicles

parts.note: to mope is to brood, so brooded is moped

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter, so only the end of the next word is kept

parts.note: final letter of useless

explanation.surface: Someone sulked over a fleet of worthless cars.
explanation.definitionFit: Mopeds are light motorised bikes, a kind of road vehicle.

clue.text: Listen to someone totally vacant in black car?

parts.note: to hear is to listen to

indicators.note: a word made totally vacant has its whole interior emptied out, leaving only its two ends

parts.note: outer letters of someone

explanation.surface: An instruction to heed a hollow-headed passenger in a dark vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A hearse is the funeral vehicle that carries a coffin, traditionally painted black, so a 'black car' by description.

clue.text: Concerning neckwear — knot again

parts.note: re means concerning, about
a tie is worn round the neck

explanation.surface: A tip about neckties: if it comes undone, tie it once more.
explanation.definitionFit: To retie is to fasten with a knot a second time, re- meaning again.

clue.text: Flag best raised to get a lot of money

parts.note: a jack is a ship's flag, as in Union Jack

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising a word lifts it bottom to top, so its letters run upwards

parts.note: top means best

explanation.surface: Hoisting the winning team's banner earns a big payout.
explanation.definitionFit: A jackpot is the top prize in a game or lottery, typically a large sum of cash.

clue.text: Eats fast and makes snide comments

definitions.meaning: first meaning: wolfs food down greedily

explanation.surface: A rude dinner guest who gobbles food and sneers at everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both gobbling food (informal) and expressing contempt by mocking remarks.

clue.text: Joyce regularly served up unusual Chilean red

indicators.note: in a down clue, sending something up makes it run bottom to top
regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter of the name is taken

parts.note: second and fourth letters of Joyce

indicators.note: unusual signals the following letters are in an unusual order

parts.note: the fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: Joyce routinely pours an odd South American red wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Red' looks like wine to go with Chilean, but it is the dye, and Chilean is anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Cochineal is a scarlet dye and food colouring made from crushed insects, so a red colourant.

clue.text: Show head justice

parts.note: a fair is a show or exhibition
a ness is a headland, as in Dungeness on the Kent coast

explanation.surface: A command to display the principal's sense of what is right.
explanation.definitionFit: Fairness is impartial and just treatment, the quality that justice embodies.

clue.text: Agitated star: is it this writer?

indicators.note: agitated means shaken up, so the letters that follow are stirred into a new order

parts.note: the fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: A celebrity, flustered, wonders whether a particular author is the one mocking them.
explanation.definitionFit: A satirist is an author who ridicules people through irony, exactly the sort to agitate a star.

clue.text: A solicitor's livelihood, perhaps, that makes for perfection?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a lawyer's business, as in a legal firm
second meaning: repeated rehearsal, from the proverb about what makes perfect

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a lawyer's career is what leads to flawlessness.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half leans on the proverb 'practice makes perfect'.
explanation.definitionFit: A professional's business is called a practice, and repeated exercise of a skill is also practice.

clue.text: Part of description needed for cast

indicators.note: part of a word is a run of its letters, so the answer sits inside the next word

parts.note: letters three to eight of description

explanation.surface: Some of the account is required for a mould or plaster cast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' suggests a plaster mould, but it is the actors in a play.
explanation.definitionFit: A script is the written text of a play, which the actors in the cast need to perform.

clue.text: Amphibian confused for good

indicators.note: confused means muddled up, so the letters of the next word are jumbled

parts.note: the fodder, taken as written
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A creature permanently bewildered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For good' reads as 'permanently'; here the two words are split into fodder and an abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A frog is a tailless leaping creature that lives both in water and on land, so an amphibian.

clue.text: Paint Mr James maybe, returning to nature

indicators.note: something returning goes back the way it came, so the name is read in reverse

parts.note: Sid James was a British comic actor of the Carry On films
temper means disposition or nature

explanation.surface: A painter named James goes back to depicting the countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: Distemper is an old-fashioned water-based paint used on walls, also called whitewash.

clue.text: Victor going topless? That's part of the target!

indicators.note: losing the top means dropping the first letter of the word it applies to

parts.note: a victor is a winner

explanation.surface: A cheeky picture of a champion stripping off and becoming the focus of attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Victor' looks like V from the phonetic alphabet, but here it means a winner, which loses its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The inner is the ring just outside the bullseye on an archery or darts board.

clue.text: Join, with an objection?

parts.note: an is the indefinite article, A
a but is an objection, as in 'no buts'

explanation.surface: Someone agrees to sign up, but only after a protest.
explanation.definitionFit: To abut is to adjoin or share a border with, so to join on at the edge.

clue.text: Reserves unlikely retail outlet

parts.note: to book is to reserve
tall as in a tall story, one hard to believe

explanation.surface: Stockpiles held by an improbable shop.
explanation.definitionFit: A bookstall is a small stand or kiosk selling books and papers, a little shop.

clue.text: Agrees to change Sierra's lubricants

indicators.note: changing the letters means arranging them differently

parts.note: fodder, taken as written
Sierra is S in the phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone consents to swap the oils in their Ford Sierra.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ford Sierra was a popular British family car, which keeps the surface in the garage.
explanation.definitionFit: Greases are thick oily lubricating substances, so the plural noun matches lubricants.

clue.text: Clever chap gathering speed — it started with rockets

indicators.note: gathering means collecting into oneself, so the first word encloses the second

parts.note: a sage is a wise man
pace means speed

explanation.surface: A brainy fellow picks up momentum on a story about early missiles.
explanation.definitionFit: The space age is the era that began with rocket launches into orbit, from Sputnik onwards.

clue.text: Display that's a bit like a trademark?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: wave or flourish to show off
second meaning, whimsically: brand plus -ish, somewhat resembling a brand

explanation.surface: A shop display that resembles a company logo.
explanation.walkthrough: The second meaning is a made-up reading: -ish means somewhat like, so 'brand-ish'.
explanation.definitionFit: To brandish is to wave something about as a show; jokingly, brand-ish is resembling a brand name.

clue.text: Character of the first noted individual?

parts.note: an individual is a person
in a list or example the first one recorded is labelled A

explanation.surface: Asking about the personality of whoever was recorded first.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay puts the individual before the label, as in 'person A'.
explanation.definitionFit: A persona is the character someone presents to the world, or a role in a drama.

clue.text: High point for Wile E. Coyote's supplier?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the peak or summit
second meaning: the fictional company whose gadgets the cartoon coyote buys

explanation.surface: The best moment for the cartoon coyote's mail-order firm.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means the peak of achievement, and Acme Corporation sells the coyote his doomed inventions in Road Runner cartoons.

clue.text: Show a prisoner in the mirror, perhaps

indicators.note: a mirror image is flipped, so the phrase is read from right to left

parts.note: taken as written
a lag is a convict, as in old lag

explanation.surface: An instruction to display a convict's reflection.
explanation.definitionFit: A gala is a festive public show or celebratory entertainment.

clue.text: Danger to blow up first of explosives — with this?

definitions.text: Danger to blow up first of explosives — with this?

indicators.note: blowing something up scatters it, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: fodder, taken as written

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter only

parts.note: opening letter of explosives

explanation.surface: A warning that the explosives could go off with the device in question.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: a hand bomb is what blows up explosives dangerously.
explanation.definitionFit: A grenade is a small thrown bomb, the very thing that would detonate dangerously among explosives.

clue.text: Fellow from a senior service, elderly

parts.note: taken as written
the Royal Navy, Britain's oldest armed service, is the Senior Service
old means elderly

explanation.surface: An aged man who served in the navy.
explanation.definitionFit: Arnold is a man's name, and crosswords often define first names as fellow, man or chap.

clue.text: Time to get drunk in the City? It'll make you sick!

indicators.note: in places the jumbled letters inside the City abbreviation

parts.note: EC is the postcode for the City of London

indicators.note: drunk means reeling and unsteady, so the letters stagger into a new order

parts.note: fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: A warning that a boozy session in the Square Mile will end in nausea.
explanation.walkthrough: The City is London's financial district, postcode EC.
explanation.definitionFit: An emetic is a substance that induces vomiting, so it makes you sick.

clue.text: Figures made from silicone snap

indicators.note: made from says the answer is formed out of letters already sitting in the next words

parts.note: letters spanning the end of silicone and the start of snap

explanation.surface: Model figurines moulded in silicone break easily.
explanation.definitionFit: A cone is a geometric solid figure, so figures in the mathematical sense.

clue.text: Lame storm possibly becoming a danger to shipping?

indicators.note: possibly suggests one arrangement among many, so the letters may be reordered

parts.note: fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: A feeble gale might still grow into something perilous for ships.
explanation.definitionFit: A maelstrom is a powerful whirlpool at sea, a real hazard for vessels.

clue.text: Food gives us hiccups, to some extent

indicators.note: to some extent means partly, so only a section of the phrase is used

parts.note: letters spanning the end of gives, all of us and the start of hiccups

explanation.surface: Complaining that a certain dish brings on hiccups.
explanation.definitionFit: Sushi is a Japanese dish of vinegared rice with raw fish, a kind of food.

clue.text: Being eaten by human? I'm alarmed

indicators.note: something eaten is swallowed inside, so the answer lies within the words that follow

parts.note: letters spanning the end of human, all of I'm and the start of alarmed

explanation.surface: Someone panics at the thought of being devoured by a person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Being eaten' reads as a passive verb, but 'Being' is a noun, the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal is a living creature, and a being is any living thing.

clue.text: Abrupt request after dinner for proof of identity?

parts.note: a curt 'pass!' asks someone to hand something over
port is the fortified wine traditionally passed round after dinner

explanation.surface: A clipped demand at the dinner table, oddly serving as ID.
explanation.walkthrough: Together the pieces form 'Pass port', a terse request at the end of a formal meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A passport is the official document proving a traveller's identity and nationality.

clue.text: Empty one's lungs: no longer fit and well

parts.note: ex means former, no longer
hale means healthy, as in hale and hearty

explanation.surface: Breathing out because one has lost one's fitness.
explanation.definitionFit: To exhale is to breathe out, expelling the air from the chest.

clue.text: Occasional table, kind of?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the chemistry chart of the elements is one type of table

explanation.walkthrough: 'Occasional table' is a piece of furniture; split apart, the words lead to an adjective and the chemistry chart.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means recurring at intervals, and the periodic table arranges the chemical elements.
